To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the credibility of websites is primarily determined by website characteristics, rather than sponsor familiarity, and (2) there is a negative relationship between the amount of information that users verify on a website and their perceived credibility of the website.

(a) perceived credibility of websites varies as a function of website genre; (b) perceived site credibility is a function of website attributes and not sponsor familiarity; and (c) self-reported information verification behavior is not a predictor of perceived credibility.

the credibility of websites depends more on the features and attributes of the site than on the reputation of the site sponsor, and that users who verify information online tend to be more experienced web users.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how users perceive the credibility of web-based content
the perceived credibility of websites, and with the role of site features (design, content, etc.) in shaping perceptions.
how individuals perceive the credibility of websites and the factors that influence these perceptions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the findings of this study support a model of perceived web credibility that is based on the credibility of a message, the credibility of a sponsor, and the credibility of a site.
the credibility of a website is determined by the extent to which a website is perceived to provide trustworthy and accurate content.
perceived web credibility is a multidimensional construct.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the more information a person can get from the site, the more credible the site is perceived.
the results of the current study support the notion that credibility judgments are primarily based on the perceived credibility attributes of websites.
we are not as good at verifying the information that we find on the internet as we think we are, but that we are getting better with experience.
The main takeaway from our work is that
credibility judgments of web-based information are not made on the basis of source familiarity, but are instead influenced by the design and content of the websites.
credibility is a complex phenomenon, and it is important to understand the relative contributions of message, site and sponsor characteristics to credibility perceptions.
people are generally not very good at assessing the credibility of websites and, therefore, should take steps to ensure that they are verifying information that is important to them.
